11. On the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under :-
Whether the deceased namely Aaisha suffered fatal injuries in a road Traffic accident dated 11.02.2017 involving vehicle bearing no. DL 3CCL 4213 driven by R- 3 and owned by R-2 and insured with R-1?

OPP. 
12. PW-1 Smt. Praveen testified that the she along with her family members was travelling in the accidental vehicle when some malfunction occurred in the left rear side wheel because of which it went out of control and collided with a tree.
She testified that her six years old daughter died lost her life in fateful accident.
Information about the incident was immediately given to the police, in pursuance of which FIR was registered and statement of all concerned were recorded.
Post Mortem examination of the deceased was also got conducted.
All the relevant documents pertaining to investigation and submissions of final report qua death by accident have been relied by the said witness in her testimony.
In cross examination, she clarified that six persons were traveling in the vehicle including two children aged 6 & 9 years.
She also stated that it was a new vehicle and therefore any malfunction was not anticipated.
She also specified that any other vehicle was not involved in the accident.
There is nothing contended by the insurance company which could raise any doubt on the testimony of the petitioner's witness.
No contrary evidence has been placed on record to infer otherwise.
MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs.
Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. & Anr
Page No. 6 of 16

The entire record of police proceedings and enquiry report has been placed on record with the conclusion that accident happened in the manner as testified without involvement of any other vehicle due to reason beyond control fo driver.
It is accordingly held that baby Aisha suffered fatal injuries in an accident involving use of accidental vehicle on the fateful day.

These two issues have been taken up together as they entail common discussion and are interconnected.
13. As claim has been sought under Section 163A MV Act, it is reproduced hereinunder for ready reference and for ease of further discussion:

(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section, "permanent disability" shall have the same meaning and extent as in the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).

Explanation: For the purpose of this sub-section, "permanent disability" shall have the same meaning and extent as in the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).
MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. & Anr Page No. 7 of 16 (2)

sentences.text: In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.
(3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule.

14. Section 163A MV Act burdens the liability of payment of fixed compensation upon owner and insurer to permanently disabled injured or to legal heir of deceased, in case of injury or death on account of accident out of use of motor vehicle.

Section 163A MV Act is founded upon "no fault"
liability principle which implies that a claim for compensation raised under Section 163A MV Act,
need not be based on pleadings or proof at the hands of the claimants, showing absence of "wrongful act", being "negligent" or "default".
15.
Accordingly, the petitioners are not required to establish on record, the aspect of ''negligence'' of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident.
What is required to be established instead is that death occurred in an accident arising out of the vehicle involved in the accident.
16. Petitioners claimed compensation u/s 163-A of the Act, only on the ground that death of victim occurred on account of accident arising out of use of accidental vehicle.

Deceased received fatal Parveen vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77621760/

sentences.text: 17. Bare perusal of Sec. 163A MV Act indicates that the compensation is payable to the victim in case of permanent disablement and to legal heirs in case of death due to accident arising out of use of motor vehicle by owner of the motor vehicle or authorised insurer as the case may be, without the claimant having to prove any negligence or default upon owner of the vehicle or any other person.
So what differentiates section 163 A MV Act from Section 166 MV Act is that claimant need not establish any negligence on the part of driver of vehicle.

18. Section 146 MV Act creates statutory liability not to use a motor vehicle unless there is a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of Chapter XI (Insurance of Motor Vehicles against Third Party Risk).
Thus a valid and effective Insurance Policy is statutorily required for meeting any liability arising out of use of said motor vehicle covering necessarily third party risks.
Section 147 MV Act postulates as to what a policy of insurance must be like to comply with the requirements of Chapter XI.

It specifies the insured to be the person or classes of person as specified in the policy to cover any liability which may be incurred by the insured in respect of death or bodily injuries to any person or damage to any property of a third party on account of use of said vehicle in a public place.

The scope of expression 'any person' in Section 147 MV Act was considered in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Asha Rani Appeal (Civil) 5385 of 2001 as also referred and relied in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited v Meena Variyal Appeal (Civil) 5825 of 2006 that it has to be understood in its context MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. &
Anr Page No. 9 of 16 and therefore use of expression any person would be qualified by the setting in which they occur and is to be understood as third party.

sentences.text: Therefore, the applicability of 163 A MV Act & 166 MV Act with respect to the classes of persons whom they cover is governed by the statutory object for which this chapter was brought in vogue, which is to cover the "third party risks".

The question now arises as to who would constitute the "third party"
in relation to a policy of insurance.
It is settled that every one other than the contracting parties to the insurance policy would be included in the expression "third party".

Noting that the prime liability under Section 163A MV Act is upon owner of the vehicle, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Rajni Appeal (Civil) 2892 of 2008 that if the said owner himself is involved in the accident, a claim under aforesaid provision would not lie.

sentences.text: It is now a well settled principle of law that in a case where third party is involved, the liability of the insurance company would be unlimited.

Where, however,
compensation is claimed for the death of the owner or another passenger of the vehicle, the contract of insurance being governed by the contract qua contract, the claim of the insurance company would depend upon the terms thereof."
21.

Therefore, if it is specified in terms of the policy that the driver of the vehicle is covered then the liability of the insurance company would not be unlimited and also not as per the amount mentioned in the Second Schedule, rather would be limited to the amount payable as per the insurance contract in such a circumstance.

Therefore, if an insurance policy is a "package policy"
and not a bare "liability only policy", it would include not only the driver but all the passengers of the vehicle.

PACKAGE POLICY:
22. A package policy is an insurance cover which, along with covering third party liabilities, offers to indemnify any damages caused to their own vehicle such as accidental damage, fire, vandalism, acts of God, natural calamities, etc.
This covers loss or damage to the vehicle insured, in addition to bodily injury and/ or death and property damage.

23. In a recent judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Sanjay Sharma Vs. New India Assurance Company, MAC App. 619/2023, a package policy basically is an insurance cover where the insurer offers protection not only against damage to third party but also personal property and physical injury to the insured as well as to other occupants in the accidental vehicle.

24. In the case at hand, minor child was travelling as one of the occupants in the accidental vehicle,
admittedly covered by a valid and effective "Private Car Package Policy" as on the date of accident.

It is a matter of record that father of the child was driving the car whereas her grand father was the owner thereof who was also travelling in the said car along with other family members when it met with an accident.

Insurance company has taken a plea that father was driving as son of owner,
having been authorised by the owner and insured to drive and therefore, he has stepped into the shoes of the owner and in such capacity liable for payment of compensation to LRs of deceased child who died in the accident whereas he himself is one of the Class -I legal heir of the said deceased child in the capacity of her father and thus, effectively the owner himself would be the beneficiary of compensation.

sentences.text: It is evident that the insurance policy is issued for occupants of the vehicle in their individual capacity and not as family members or legal heirs of owner or driver or insured.

Any other interpretation would lead to an anomalous situation as in majority of cases, the car would be carrying family members of MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. & Anr Page No. 12 of 16 owner or insured only, which would render the 'package policy' as practically redundant most of the times.

entities.text: MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. & Anr

sentences.text: The 'package policy' evidently, does not make any exclusion of the family members of owner or insured.

Similarly, the circular of (TAC ) mentions the inclusion as 'other occupants in the car' therefore, it only has attempted to carve out a distinction between the driver of the car and the other occupants irrespective of they being the owner or insured or any legal heirs thereof.
Victim was an occupant of the car when it met with an accident.
She was in no position to control what happened in the accident which claimed her life.
The insurance contract of the accidental vehicle provides coverage for life of occupants of the car.
There is nothing mentioned by the insurance company to restrict the liability of compensation towards the occupants of the accidental vehicle to a particular limited amount.

It is thus held that the insurance company as the authorised insurer of the accidental vehicle is liable to pay compensation for the death of Baby Aisha, caused by the use of accidental motor vehicle as per the terms of contract of Policy of Insurance.
The only claimant in this matter is mother of Baby Aisha who is neither the driver nor the owner of the accidental vehicle.
26. It is held that the petitioner has been able to prove her entitlement for compensation under Section 163A MV Act against the death of her six year old child in a motor vehicle accident.
In view of the notification issued by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways dated 22.05.2018, the claimant/ mother of deceased is entitled for an amount of Rs. 5.0 lakhs.

31.
Mother of deceased is the only claimant in this matter.

32. The observations made in case of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in N. Jayashree & Ors. Vs.
Cholamandlam MS Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd, SLP (C) no.14558 of 2019 relevant in this context:
"14.The MV Act does not define the term 'legal representative'.

entities.text:
N. Jayashree & Ors. Vs.
Cholamandlam MS Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd, SLP (C) no.14558 of 2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Generally, 'legal representative' means a person who in law represents the estate of the deceased person and includes any person or persons in whom legal right to receive compensatory benefit vests.
A 'legal representative' may also include any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased.
Such person does not necessarily have to be a legal heir.

Legal heirs are the persons who are entitled to inherit the surviving estate of the deceased..."
33. Section 163 A MC Act entitles only the legal heirs of deceased to receive compensation unlike legal representative MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. & Anr Page No.
15 of 16 under Section 166 MV Act.
It is thus held that claimant / mother being class -I legal heir of deceased is entitled to receive compensation.

Section 163A MV Act is founded upon "no fault"
liability principle which implies that a claim for compensation raised under Section 163A MV Act,
need not be based on pleadings or proof at the hands of the claimants, showing absence of "wrongful act", being "negligent" or "default".
15.
Accordingly, the petitioners are not required to establish on record, the aspect of ''negligence'' of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident.
What is required to be established instead is that death occurred in an accident arising out of the vehicle involved in the accident.
16. Petitioners claimed compensation u/s 163-A of the Act, only on the ground that death of victim occurred on account of accident arising out of use of accidental vehicle.
So neither was she owner nor driver of vehicle so MACT No. 456/2017 Praveen & Anr. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. & Anr Page No. 8 of 16 compensation is not being sought for injury or death on account of her own negligence.
17. Bare perusal of Sec. 163A MV Act indicates that the compensation is payable to the victim in case of permanent disablement and to legal heirs in case of death due to accident arising out of use of motor vehicle by owner of the motor vehicle or authorised insurer as the case may be, without the claimant having to prove any negligence or default upon owner of the vehicle or any other person.
So what differentiates section 163 A MV Act from Section 166 MV Act is that claimant need not establish any negligence on the part of driver of vehicle.
Thus a valid and effective Insurance Policy is statutorily required for meeting any liability arising out of use of said motor vehicle covering necessarily third party risks.
It is settled that every one other than the contracting parties to the insurance policy would be included in the expression "third party".
19. The above judgment was also referred and relied in the Landmark Judgment on the subject as titled as Ningamma & Anr Vs United India Insurance Company Civil Appeal No. 3538 of 2009,
Dhanraj v. New India Assurance Co. (2004) 8 SCC 553, New India Assurance Company Limited Vs.
Sadanand Mukhi Civil Appeal no. 7402 of 2008.
20.
Therefore, if it is specified in terms of the policy that the driver of the vehicle is covered then the liability of the insurance company would not be unlimited and also not as per the amount mentioned in the Second Schedule, rather would be limited to the amount payable as per the insurance contract in such a circumstance.
Therefore, if an insurance policy is a "package policy"
and not a bare "liability only policy", it would include not only the driver but all the passengers of the vehicle.
PACKAGE POLICY:
22. A package policy is an insurance cover which, along with covering third party liabilities, offers to indemnify any damages caused to their own vehicle such as accidental damage, fire, vandalism, acts of God, natural calamities, etc.
This covers loss or damage to the vehicle insured, in addition to bodily injury and/ or death and property damage.
Insurance company has taken a plea that father was driving as son of owner,
having been authorised by the owner and insured to drive and therefore, he has stepped into the shoes of the owner and in such capacity liable for payment of compensation to LRs of deceased child who died in the accident whereas he himself is one of the Class -I legal heir of the said deceased child in the capacity of her father and thus, effectively the owner himself would be the beneficiary of compensation.

It is evident that the insurance policy is issued for occupants of the vehicle in their individual capacity and not as family members or legal heirs of owner or driver or insured.
In view of the notification issued by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways dated 22.05.2018, the claimant/ mother of deceased is entitled for an amount of Rs. 5.0 lakhs.
In the present case, the vehicle was owned by respondent no.2/Shahid Ali.

opennyai_summary.decision:
It is directed that a compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rs. Five Lakhs only) is awarded to the petitioners along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization of the actual amount.
It is thus held that claimant / mother being class -I legal heir of deceased is entitled to receive compensation.
RELEASE /DISBURSEMENT OF AWARD AMOUNT 34.
The total compensation amount is released in favour of claimant / mother of deceased in her bank account near her place of residence without any pre condition of FDR.
35. Copy of this award be given to the parties free of cost.
The copy of award be sent to the DLSA and Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate.
36. The case is now fixed for compliance by the insurance Digitally company for 14.10.2024.
